newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Peru Yauliyacu transfer now to take place Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: Peru Yauliyacu transfer now to take place Feb 28.

text.p: The transfer of Peruvian polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu to Brazil's Paranapanema will now take place on February 28, said Paranapanema's finance and market relations' director.
"It is now scheduled for February 28. The bureaucratic problems are being resolved," said Helio Blak.

Paranapanema bought Yauliyacu for $12.7 million at auction last December from Peruvian state miner Centromin. The formal transfer was scheduled for February 18 but was delayed due to the non-arrival of some documents.
The Paranapanema group which was formed last year includes copper producer Caraiba Metais, zinc unit Companhia Paraibuna de Metais and tin producer Mamore (formerly known as Paranapanema).

The group plans to invest almost $100 million this year, of which $15 million will be spent improving and increasing production of Caraiba to 202,000 tonnes in 1998 from 192,000 tonnes this year, Blak said.
Another $32 million will be invested in increasing capacity at the group's semi-finished copper goods unit, Eluma to 47,000 tonnes, 46.9 percent more than last year.
Output at Mamore is also expected to rise to 17,000 tonnes in 1997 from 12,000 tonnes after investments of $16 million.
Paraibuna meanwhile will receive $3.3 million to boost output to 75,000 tonnes from 62,000 tonnes.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
